findings.desc: Docs describe dispatch_auto as starting only after host unattended-safety checks pass, but the reusable probe fact never becomes true for Claude and the scheduler bypasses it with a Claude-specific subset check. This keeps v1.0.1 behavior conservative enough, but leaves the host-neutral safety boundary under-specified for future hosts/extensions.

CHK-002:edge:0 overclaims explicit opt-in coverage. The intent requires that a claude-code policy without allowRealHostSubprocess=true stays supervised/refused for real subprocess launch, but the recorded evidence points to dispatch-run-smoke paths that only cover host-not-in-policy and gemini unavailable/unattendedSafe=false refusals, not the dedicated claude-code missing-opt-in branch. The production code has a separate refusal at lattice-dispatch.ts:2747-2750, yet unattended-dispatch-smoke only exercises allowRealHostSubprocess=true success/env/nonzero/timeout cases.
